subject: SEV-1: NovaRetail checkout inference degradation — exec update & bridge
messages:
From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com, evelyn_hart@redwood.com, emily.turner@novaretail.com
Cc: ops@novaretail.com
Date: 2026-03-22T09:12:00Z
Subject: SEV-1: Production inference degradation impacting NovaRetail Checkout

Team and NovaRetail ops,

We’re seeing a production degradation that’s affecting real-time LLM responses for NovaRetail’s checkout flow (inference timeouts and elevated 5xx). Customer reports began at ~09:05 UTC; our telemetry shows error rates spiking at 09:03 UTC. Impact: higher cart abandonment for a subset of requests routed to the low-latency endpoint.

Immediate actions taken:
- Shifted NovaRetail traffic to fallback model variant (v2-512q) to reduce timeouts.
- Throttled background batch jobs that were contending for GPU pools.
- On-call is collecting logs and a timeline (attached: incident-bridge-log.txt).

Planned next steps (next 30–60m):
- Open incident bridge for engineering + customer ops at 09:30 UTC (link to follow).
- Prepare an executive-facing note for NovaRetail leadership summarizing impact and ETA for mitigation (I’ll draft).
- Triage root cause: kernel scheduling anomalies vs. model cache corruption.

Marissa, can you confirm the bridge attendees and whether we want to authorize immediate credits if the workaround (fallback model) degrades output quality? Emily, we’ll keep you updated on the bridge link — apologies for the disruption.

-Markus
---
Markus Klein
VP, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Emily Turner <emily.turner@novaretail.com>, NovaRetail CSO <cso@novaretail.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, markus_klein@redwood.com, evelyn_hart@redwood.com
Date: 2026-03-22T10:05:00Z
Subject: Executive update: NovaRetail SEV-1 — current status and next steps

Emily / NovaRetail leadership —

I’m Jonas Weber, SVP Customer Experience at Redwood. I wanted to provide a concise executive update following the bridge we just completed. First, sincere apologies for the interruption to your checkout flow; we know every minute matters.

What happened (current understanding):
- At ~09:03 UTC an internal scheduling regression in our GPU runtime caused increased contention for the low-latency inference pool handling NovaRetail traffic. This led to elevated tail latencies and intermittent 5xx responses for a portion of requests.

Mitigation performed (completed):
- Traffic shifted to a verified fallback model variant (v2-512q) to restore throughput and reduce timeouts.
- Background GPU-heavy batch jobs were paused to free capacity.
- We have begun a controlled restart of the scheduler with a throttled config; initial results show error rate declining.

Current status (10:05 UTC):
- Majority of affected requests are responding; error rate has fallen from peak ~24% to ~3% on your routed endpoints.
- We expect steady recovery to normal within the next 45–90 minutes as the scheduler stabilizes and caches rebuild.

Customer impact and compensation:
- We regret the customer experience and are prepared to offer NovaRetail a credit for the incident window. Marissa will follow up with a proposed credit based on observed RTT/failed request delta and the terms of your contract (Deal ID: NR-ENT-5821).

Postmortem & follow-up:
- We will deliver a draft postmortem within 72 hours with timeline, root cause analysis, and corrective actions. Final postmortem with code fixes and release date will follow within 14 days. Attachment: postmortem-skeleton.md (outline and proposed ownership).

Immediate asks for NovaRetail ops:
1) Please confirm if the fallback model output quality is acceptable for your checkout UX (we can revert to primary once you sign off).
2) If you prefer a technical runbook call, we can schedule a 1:1 deep dive with your engineering leads.

We appreciate your patience. I’ll personally own the follow-up until this is resolved and ensure transparent updates.

Best,
Jonas Weber
SVP, Customer Experience
Redwood Inference
